cards.name: Fruit
cards.summary: Swatch library of 79 CMYK process colours in 19 colour groups (Apple, Banana, Blueberry, Citrus 1, Citrus 2, Durian, Fig, Fruit Cocktail, Lemon, Lemon-Lime, Lime, Mangosteen and 7 more). The strip shows a loud mix of fruit colours: crimson, hot pink and magenta, tomato red and orange, lemon and banana yellows, lime and neon greens, blueberry blues, plum purples, olive and tan browns, with a few pale cream cells, one white and two pure black cells. (Thumbnail: a swatch strip drawn by script from the file's colour values, not a shipped preview.)
use_for: fruit stand, juice bar or smoothie branding
kids' food packaging or recipe cards
avoid: calm corporate or editorial layouts: very saturated and varied; use Neutral or Corporate
picking single swatches blindly: the colours are organised by fruit group (Apple, Banana, Lime...); take a whole group
RGB screen work needing exact hex values: these are CMYK process colours and shift on conversion
cards.applies_to: an open document (the library opens as its own panel); its swatches set the fill or stroke of selected paths, shapes, type and groups, and its colour groups can be added to the document's Swatches panel or used in Recolor Artwork
cards.how_to_apply: Panel: Window > Swatch Libraries > Foods > Fruit; with objects selected click a swatch to set fill or stroke, or select a colour group folder and choose Add to Swatches from the library panel menu. Script: no loader call was harvested (invoke holds only the .ase file), so recreate the colours from the harvested values, e.g. var c = new CMYKColor(); c.cyan = 30; c.magenta = 98; c.yellow = 86; c.black = 2; var s = doc.swatches.add(); s.name = 'C=30 M=98 Y=86 K=2 1'; s.color = c; (group them with doc.swatchGroups.add().addSwatch(s)).

verified.note: Grid of 79 flat CMYK fruit colours (crimson, pinks, oranges, yellows, limes, blues, purples, olives) including two pure black cells and one white cell.

review.changes: summary said one pure black; the strip has two black cells and a white one

Script: no loader call was harvested (invoke holds only the .ase file), so recreate the colours from the harvested values, e.g. var c = new CMYKColor(); c.cyan = 0; c.magenta = 0; c.yellow = 10; c.black = 30; var s = doc.swatches.add(); s.name = 'C=0 M=0 Y=10 K=30'; s.color = c; (group them with doc.swatchGroups.add().addSwatch(s)).

verified.note: Flat muted neutrals: sage, blue-grey, khaki, taupe, charcoal, near-black, browns, dusty rose, cream and sand.

cards.name: Basic Graphics_Dots
cards.summary: Pattern swatch library file (CMYK document, 25 entries): [None], [Registration] and 23 pattern swatches (10 dpi and 6 dpi dot screens from 10% to 90%, 0 to 50%, 0 to 100% and 50% to 100% Dot Gradation, Undulating Coarse Dots and Undulating Fine Dots). The strip shows black dots on white as halftone-style screens: small dots through large dots across the 10% to 90% steps at two dot sizes, dot gradations that grow across the tile, and undulating coarse and fine dot waves; some tiles show white dots knocked out of black squares. (Thumbnail: a swatch strip drawn by script from the library file's own entries, [None] and [Registration] not drawn; not a shipped preview.)
use_for: tonal shading in one-colour or black-and-white illustration
avoid: colour work: the patterns are black; edit the pattern swatch to change its colour
tiny output sizes: the 10 dpi dots turn to grey mush when scaled down
